definition: LoRA fine-tuning applied to a base model stored in low precision (4-bit), making full fine-tuning affordable on a single GPU.
details: QLoRA backpropagates through a frozen, 4-bit quantized model while training small LoRA adapters, and adds paged optimizers and double quantization to cut memory further. It demonstrated that a 65-billion-parameter model could be fine-tuned on a single 48 GB GPU with quality rivaling full fine-tuning.

explainer.lead: QLoRA applies LoRA fine-tuning to a base model stored in 4-bit precision, making full fine-tuning affordable on a single GPU. It matters because it brought 65-billion-parameter fine-tuning within reach of one 48 GB GPU.

tiers.eli5: Like retraining a huge model while it is squeezed into a smaller package, so it fits on one machine.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers backpropagate through a frozen 4-bit quantised model while training small LoRA adapters, adding paged optimizers and double quantization to cut memory further; the pitfall is that the quantisation must still preserve quality.
tiers.paperLevel: QLoRA trains LoRA adapters on a frozen model stored in 4-bit, with paged optimizers and double quantization reducing memory; it showed a 65-billion-parameter model could be fine-tuned on one 48 GB GPU with quality rivaling full fine-tuning.

explainer.example: A team fine-tunes a 65-billion-parameter model on a single 48 GB GPU by training only small adapters over the 4-bit base.

citation.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
citation.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36 (NeurIPS)
